fact: Winter 2022-23 was a La Nina winter. North India was remarkably clean, with PM2.5 down by up to 30% from the 2019-22 average.
source: TOI, 'Study traces how an El Nino changed the pollution map'

fact: In winter 2022-23 peninsular India was considerably dirtier; average PM2.5 in Mumbai rose by 45%.
source: TOI article on the ENSO pollution study

fact: In winter 2023-24 (El Nino) the pattern reversed: PM2.5 spiralled in the north (Jaipur up about 50%, Delhi up over 10% vs the 2019-22 average) and fell sharply in peninsular India.
source: TOI article on the ENSO pollution study

fact: Year-to-year PM2.5 changes ranged from about a 40% decline to a 70% increase versus the 2019-22 average, despite no major change in emissions or pollution-control policies.
source: TOI article on the ENSO pollution study

fact: Under La Nina, stronger winds over north India dispersed emissions from stubble burning and local sources; circulation bypassed Delhi and carried pollutants south to cities such as Mumbai and Thiruvananthapuram.
source: TOI article citing the study in Atmospheric Pollution Research

fact: Under El Nino, winds over northern India were weaker and passed through Delhi and Jaipur instead of carrying pollutants away, so stagnation favoured PM2.5 build-up.
source: TOI article citing the study in Atmospheric Pollution Research

fact: Rainfall was more strongly linked to lower PM2.5 in 2022-23; in 2023-24 surface pressure mattered more (high pressure, weak winds and a shallow boundary layer trap pollutants near the ground).
source: TOI article on the ENSO pollution study

fact: Backward air-mass trajectories showed Jaipur kept receiving air from polluted northern regions in the El Nino winter, while Hyderabad received cleaner marine and southern air.
source: TOI article on the ENSO pollution study

fact: For Delhi-NCR, low local or agricultural emissions do not automatically guarantee cleaner air if large-scale circulation turns stagnant; conversely, high emissions can have a smaller local impact when strong winds disperse them.
source: TOI article on the ENSO pollution study

fact: The authors caution that the correlations neither establish direct causality nor can be extrapolated to other years, and that El Nino does not invariably worsen air quality in Delhi or north India. Only two unusual winters were studied.
source: TOI article on the ENSO pollution study

fact: Gufran Beig, a study author, said this year's El Nino is likely to be the strongest on record, but the authors are not implying the 2023-24 pattern will repeat this winter.
source: TOI article on the ENSO pollution study

fact: In northwest India the hot semi-arid zone grew from about a quarter of the region in 1951-60 to a third in 1991-2020, while the temperate zone shrank from about a quarter to under a fifth.
source: TOI article on the IMD/IITM climate-zone study

fact: The hot, dry zone has pushed east into Uttar Pradesh, one of India's most important farming regions, so the timing of sowing and harvesting needs to be watched closely (lead author Ananya Karmakar, IMD and IITM).
source: TOI article on the IMD/IITM climate-zone study

fact: In peninsular India the hot semi-arid zone shrank from about 30% of the region to 16%, mostly becoming tropical savannah (now about three-quarters of the peninsula), attributed to rising rainfall over southern India. Marathwada and west Vidarbha moved into the hot semi-arid zone.
source: TOI article on the IMD/IITM climate-zone study

fact: The climate-zone study could be handy for farm-sector policymakers.
source: TOI article on the IMD/IITM climate-zone study

fact: WHO 2021 air-quality guideline for PM2.5: 5 ug/m3 annual mean and 15 ug/m3 24-hour mean.
source: WHO global air quality guidelines 2021 - VERIFY

fact: India's National Ambient Air Quality Standards for PM2.5 are 40 ug/m3 annual and 60 ug/m3 24-hour.

The National Clean Air Programme (launched 2019) sets city-level PM targets for non-attainment cities, and the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) coordinates action across Delhi-NCR and adjoining states.
